question: A person lends ₹20,000 at 12% simple interest per annum. What will be the interest earned in 2.5 years?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net interest percentage = Rate × Time

Net Interest % = 12% × 2.5 = 30%

Interest earned = 30% of ₹20,000 = 0.30 × 20,000

Interest earned = ₹6,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹6,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given:

Principal (P) = ₹20,000

Rate of Interest (R) = 12% per annum

Time (T) = 2.5 years

Formula Used: Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) / 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0cb230d9c5cee5dbeb744826b57f828d0f705d4e3e2d01dfd99c97e0ba4d114c.png] 

Calculations:

⇒ SI = (20000 × 12 × 2.5) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 200 × 12 × 2.5

⇒ SI = 200 × 30

⇒ SI = ₹6,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹6,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Amount Calculation

The total amount (A) to be paid back after the time period is the sum of the principal and the interest: A = P + SI.

Simple Interest vs. Compound Interest

In simple interest, the principal remains constant throughout the period, whereas in compound interest, interest is calculated on the updated principal (P + previous interest) every cycle.

Calculating Time or Rate

From the SI formula, we can derive: T = (SI × 100) ÷ (P × R) and R = (SI × 100) ÷ (P × T).
